description: Decision-replay cases for comparing the pre-v1.2 and candidate v1.2 governance protocols.

cases.title: T/CC anchors were omitted from the canonical backbone
cases.scenario: A production projection had separate R/G and T/CC seed writers. T/CC changed anchors were treated as support, so the rendered structural graph could be empty even though the PR changed code.
cases.notes: The historical PR itself records one canonical seed authority and a counterexample for the empty graph. The protocol comparison tests whether the governance model would surface the authority transition before mutation.

cases.title: Evaluation of LLM shadow mappings needed a separate authority
cases.scenario: A typed, deterministic evaluation result was added for recorded LLM shadow observations. The evaluator had to remain consumer-local and must not become formal review authority or invoke a provider.
cases.notes: The historical record explicitly separates the evaluation sink from the CLI execution authority and formal assessment.

cases.title: Collapsed structural overview changed only a presentation projection
cases.scenario: The HTML overview was narrowed to changed files and true retained bridges while the canonical graph, focus association, assessment, and full audit remained authoritative.
cases.notes: This is both a historical failure analogue and a boundary test: a correct local projection must not be promoted to domain-wide structural truth.

cases.title: Canonical backbone projection with bounded membership
cases.scenario: A stable projection invariant was supported by counterexamples, sink evidence, bounded incident relations, ownership ancestors, and tests that preserved the complete graph while laying out a canonical backbone.
cases.notes: This positive control checks that v1.2 does not reject an already well-bounded invariant or demand unnecessary planning bureaucracy.

cases.title: Helper and layout cleanup with no semantic plan change
cases.scenario: A refactor moves local helpers and adjusts report layout while preserving the same output authority, contracts, selected region, and sinks.
cases.notes: This case is held out from the historical examples and tests the explicit v1.2 exemption for changes that leave the semantic plan intact.

cases.title: Consumer-local presentation summary remains local
cases.scenario: A report-only summary groups canonical evidence for readability, records its presentation-local owner, and does not write back to graph membership, assessment, coverage, or acceptance.
cases.notes: This negative control is intentionally safe: the correct decision is to keep the projection local, not to add a new cross-consumer authority.

cases.title: Execution evidence changes the semantic owner after planning
cases.scenario: After a plan assigns one module as the canonical producer, an injected repository fact shows that the intended sink is owned by a different module. The agent must stop production-boundary mutation, revise the plan, and re-check affected contracts and merge evidence.
cases.notes: This is the execution-time injection required by #270. It is a deterministic decision replay, not a claim that a live coding agent has been statistically tested.
